item.title: Sesshu Garden, Yamaguchi: A Zen Master's Design — Guide
item.description: The garden known as Sesshu Teien, in the grounds of Joei-ji temple in Yamaguchi city, is traditionally attributed to Sesshu Toyo, the fifteenth-century painter-monk regarded as one of the greatest masters of Japanese ink painting. Laid out as a strolling and viewing garden behind the temple, it composes moss, carefully placed stones, clipped shrubs and a quiet pond into a serene landscape meant to be contemplated much like one of Sesshu’s paintings.
